rationale:
TRIAGE: All candidates are direct-label matches (AAA) but differ in what their reported performance likely represents (PRS-only vs full-model), validation scale, and covariate packaging.

Shortlist (close comparison warranted):
- PGS003973: Very strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.882, with CI) and explicit conventional covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex). Even if this is not PRS-only, it is strong direct-endpoint predictive evidence and could dominate; needs head-to-head scrutiny against cleaner PRS-only metrics elsewhere.
- PGS001784: Clean PRS-only metric available (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.014661) plus very large validation N (350,767). Also reports a high AUROC (0.868) but likely full-model; still, the presence of a PRS-only R2 makes it a key comparator and a potential “cleaner-metric” alternative to PGS003973.
- PGS003429: Direct AAA score in a screening/cost-effectiveness context; reports AUROC 0.708 (CI) and R2 0.00547 (likely model-level/packaged). Covariates are “Unknown,” which could mislead a single-shot picker (unclear whether metrics are PRS-only). Keep for comparison because it is purpose-built for a downstream use-case and has explicit uncertainty intervals.
- PGS003972: Same publication family/method/variant count as PGS003973 (PRS-CS; 1,118,997 variants) but much lower reported AUROC (0.69) and smaller validation N (6,940). This sibling contrast is exactly the kind of situation that can mislead a single-shot picker; keep both siblings on the shortlist to resolve endpoint/metric differences.

Watchlist (plausible but likely secondary unless shortlist evidence is ambiguous):
- PGS002054: Has a comparable-ish PRS-only-style metric (partial correlation 0.0144) and very large training N (391,124) with multi-ancestry evaluation. However, the metric is not directly comparable to AUROC/C-index and may be easy to over/under-interpret; keep as a portability-focused alternative.
- PGS000753: Small-variant P+T score (29 variants) with an OR 1.37 (CI) and moderate validation N (46,564). Could be robust/clinically interpretable but may underperform genome-wide PRS; keep as a “simpler model” comparator and because effect-size-only reporting can mislead if treated as equivalent to discrimination metrics. Uncertainty: Key ambiguity is metric packaging: several candidates report AUROC/C-index that may be full-model (with covariates) rather than PRS-only, and covariates are missing/unknown for some records. The two Nat Genet siblings (PGS003972 vs PGS003973) likely differ by endpoint definition/time-to-event framing or evaluation setup, but that is not visible here; downstream comparison should explicitly reconcile what each reported metric conditions on and whether it is directly comparable. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with phenotype-aligned endpoints (all report abdominal aortic aneurysm; one specifies prevalent AAA but remains aligned). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the set is PGS000753’s per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program), with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and multi-ancestry evaluation reported. Competing models largely provide only full-model discrimination metrics (e.g., AUROC/C-index) that are not clearly PRS-only and/or come from framework/portability-style papers (PGS001784, PGS002054), making cross-model performance comparison unreliable; the very high C-index for PGS003973 is especially hard to interpret as PRS contribution because it is reported with age/sex covariates and lacks PRS-only metrics. Because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC across the pool and several metrics are likely full-model, the selection is supported but not definitive, lowering confidence to Moderate and the outcome to DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL. PICK: All candidates are direct-label matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm, so the decision turns on strength/interpretability of the visible predictive evidence plus evaluation scale and covariate packaging.

PGS003973 is clearly best-supported on multiple independent visible axes: (1) it reports the strongest discrimination-type metric in the pool with uncertainty (C-index 0.882, 95% CI 0.872–0.892) on the direct endpoint; (2) it uses conventional, clearly stated covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) rather than unknown packaging; and (3) it comes from a large multi-cohort AAA meta-analysis context with a reasonable external validation size (n=7,517). While the C-index is likely a full-model metric (so not purely PRS-only), that same limitation applies to most competitors’ AUROC/C-index reporting here; given the magnitude and the presence of a CI plus ordinary covariates, it remains the strongest visible predictive evidence overall.

The legacy pick (PGS000753) is defensible (direct endpoint; clean per-SD OR=1.37 with CI; standard covariates; decent validation n=46,564), but it is a much smaller-variant P+T score and lacks any discrimination/R2 reporting, making it harder to argue it is better-supported than PGS003973 when a much stronger discrimination signal is available.

Runner-ups: PGS001784 has the cleanest PRS-only-style metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.014661) and very large validation (n=350,767), but its headline AUROC (0.868) is also likely full-model and its covariate set is more complex; overall it is competitive but not clearly stronger than PGS003973 on endpoint-aligned predictive evidence. PGS000753 remains a solid simpler alternative with interpretable effect size evidence.

Therefore, revising away from the legacy proposal is warranted because PGS003973 is clearly better-supported across multiple visible axes (stronger discrimination with CI + conventional covariates + direct endpoint), not merely because of cleaner PRS-only metric formatting. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed_pick (PGS003973). All candidates are direct AAA matches by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, so selection hinges on visible predictive evidence and packaging. PGS003973 has the strongest visible discrimination metric in the pool (C-index 0.882 with CI) on the direct endpoint, with conventional covariates explicitly listed (Age, Age^2, Sex) and a reasonable validation N (7,517). While this is likely a full-model metric (not PRS-only), the same ambiguity affects most AUROC/C-index reports here; nothing visible contradicts using it as the best-supported predictive evidence.

Legacy proposal (PGS000753) is defensible as a direct AAA score with a clear per-SD OR=1.37 (CI) and standard covariates, but it lacks any discrimination/R2 reporting and is a 29-variant P+T model; given the presence of a much stronger endpoint-aligned discrimination metric with uncertainty (PGS003973), the legacy pick is not as well-supported as the proposed_pick. No alternative candidate is clearly better-supported than PGS003973 on the visible fields: PGS001784 has a clean PRS-only R2 (0.014661) and huge validation N, but its AUROC is also likely full-model and its covariate set is more complex; PGS003429/PGS003972 show materially lower AUROC (~0.708/0.69). Therefore keep proposed_pick and do not revert to legacy.

TRIAGE: Plan for downstream head-to-head comparison should center on three distinct “archetypes” that could plausibly win depending on endpoint/ancestry priorities and how metrics are interpreted.

1) PGS002738 (AUD; EUR eval; OR top10% vs rest=1.96 [1.54–2.51]; n=7,900) is a strong direct-endpoint candidate for the target trait label (alcohol dependence/AUD). It has clear case-control style discrimination evidence (top-decile OR) and a reasonably large EUR validation sample. Potentially misleading aspect for single-shot picking: covariates are listed as Unknown and the record has multiple performance entries (record_count=4) but only one metric is surfaced here, so downstream comparison should verify which evaluation setting/adjustments correspond to the reported OR and whether results are consistent across the multiple entries.

2) PGS000201 (problematic alcohol use / AUD DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed; ΔR²=0.01192; β=0.099; n=7,599; EUR eval) is a strong near-tie despite being a measurement/count phenotype rather than a binary AUD label. It has relatively clean covariate reporting (sex, age, PCs, array, site) and a comparable-sized validation sample to PGS002738. Potentially misleading aspect: the metric is ΔR² vs covariates (continuous outcome framing) rather than an OR/AUC, so naive comparison against OR-based candidates can over/understate relative predictive utility; keep it for careful apples-to-apples reasoning rather than discarding.

3) PGS002739 (AUD; AFR eval; OR top10% vs rest=1.76 [1.32–2.34]; n=6,315; PRS-CSx gene-based; 858 variants) deserves close comparison as a strong ancestry-specific alternative with direct AUD endpoint evidence. It could be incorrectly downweighted by a single-shot picker due to smaller variant count or because its evaluation ancestry differs from the EUR-evaluated candidates; conversely it could be incorrectly overweighted if one assumes gene-based/PRS-CSx implies superiority without comparable metric context. Keep it on the shortlist for explicit ancestry-transportability discussion.

PGS000202 (same publication family as PGS000201; ΔR²=0.00456; β=0.043; n=1,251) is a plausible sibling alternative but looks visibly weaker on the reported incremental variance explained and has a much smaller validation sample. It remains worth a watchlist slot because it is a “clean-metric/clean-covariate” style comparator within the same study family, but it is less likely to beat PGS000201 unless downstream inspection reveals materially different evaluation design or phenotype alignment advantages not visible here. Uncertainty: Key uncertainties that could change the downstream ordering: (a) lack of visible AUC/R² in a common scale across all candidates (OR-top-decile vs ΔR² vs β), (b) covariates and packaging are Unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 so the reported ORs may reflect different adjustment/analysis contexts than the ΔR² records, (c) endpoint alignment differences (binary AUD vs DSM-5 criteria count) may matter depending on the intended target definition, and (d) ancestry match to the intended deployment population could dominate the decision, especially for PGS002739 (AFR eval) versus the EUR-evaluated scores. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept via alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder: PGS002738 and PGS002739 have trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201 and PGS000202 are labeled "Problematic alcohol use" but their phenotyping_reported is also AUD (DSM-5 criteria count), supporting endpoint alignment. Among these, PGS002738 is best supported because it matches the target EFO exactly (alcohol dependence), uses a standard genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), is developed in a multi-cohort context (MVP, UKB), and reports a relatively strong discrimination-relevant effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, covariates are unknown for PGS002738 (reducing comparability), and the alternative PGS000201 reports a modest incremental ΔR² (0.01192) with explicit covariates, making the ranking not definitive. PICK: Keeping the legacy pick is defensible on the visible records. All candidates are reasonably direct to the target concept (alcohol dependence/AUD), but PGS002738 is the most straightforward direct-endpoint match (trait_efo="alcohol dependence", phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder") with the strongest directly interpretable case/control-style predictive evidence shown here: OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR validation (n=7,900), and it is developed in a multi-cohort context (MVP, UKB) using a standard PRS-CS approach. 

PGS000201 is a credible near-tie because its phenotyping is also AUD (DSM-5 criteria count) with explicit conventional covariates and similar validation N (n=7,599), but its visible performance is ΔR²=0.01192 on a (log-transformed) criteria-count outcome, which is harder to compare directly against the OR-based discrimination evidence and does not clearly exceed PGS002738 on predictive signal. PGS002739 is similarly direct on endpoint and shows a solid OR (1.76 [1.32–2.34]) but is evaluated in AFR ancestry (n=6,315), making it less generally supported as the single best pick absent an explicit AFR deployment context. PGS000202 appears weaker on visible signal (smaller ΔR²=0.00456 and much smaller validation n=1,251). 

Limitations remain (no PRS-only AUC/R² for any candidate; covariates unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739; PGS002738 has multiple performance entries not fully surfaced), so the outcome stays DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed pick. PGS002738 is a defensible best choice on visible evidence: it is directly aligned to the target concept (trait_efo="alcohol dependence", phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"), has a sizable EUR validation sample (n=7,900), and reports the strongest directly interpretable discrimination-style metric among candidates (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51). Alternatives are not clearly better-supported: PGS000201 has clean covariates and similar N but only ΔR²=0.01192 on a log-transformed DSM-5 criteria count (harder to compare to OR and not obviously stronger); PGS002739 is also direct but is AFR-evaluated (n=6,315) and has a lower OR (1.76); PGS000202 is visibly weaker (smaller ΔR² and much smaller n=1,251). Covariates are Unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 and PGS002738 has multiple performance entries not surfaced, but these are uncertainty factors rather than contradictions that would force a revision. The legacy_with_domain_proposal matches the proposed_pick and is likewise defensible, so keep_legacy_proposal=true.

TRIAGE: All three candidates are close enough on endpoint alignment (all map to alcoholic liver cirrhosis) but differ in study archetype, metric packaging, and scale in ways that could mislead a single-shot picker; they therefore all deserve head-to-head downstream comparison.

- PGS000704: Very large training (UKB) and large validation N with a time-to-event framing (C-index 0.711; HR reported). However, the reported performance is a full model with covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), not PRS-only, so apparent strength could partly reflect packaging; still, the scale/robustness and direct endpoint label make it a strong contender.

- PGS004913: Most directly “on-construct” for the intended use context (alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers) and has relatively clean conventional covariates listed (age/sex/PCs). Metrics are not AUC but include R²=0.029 and an OR (top vs bottom deciles) with wide CI; smaller training/validation than UKB but purpose-built endpoint definition makes it a strong direct-endpoint alternative to compare against the UKB-derived model.

- PGS001777: Very small variant count (3) and small validation N, but reports an AUROC (0.671) and a large stratification OR (top 20% vs bottom 20%). Phenotyping_reported indicates a sex-stratified endpoint (“Cirrhosis (males)”) and covariates are unknown, so comparability/packaging is unclear; nonetheless, the strong effect-size-style stratification metric could look compelling in isolation, so it should be retained for careful downstream scrutiny rather than dropped at triage. Uncertainty: Cross-candidate comparability is limited because metrics are heterogeneous (C-index/HR vs AUROC vs R²/decile OR) and several are full-model or have unclear covariate packaging. Endpoint definitions also differ subtly (general alcoholic cirrhosis vs heavy-drinker-focused vs sex-stratified), which could drive performance differences independent of PRS quality. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned phenotyping labels. PGS001777 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused study explicitly about alcohol-related cirrhosis risk prediction and provides a clear discrimination metric (full-model AUROC 0.671) plus a strong stratification effect size (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41), supporting meaningful risk separation despite using only 3 variants. Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the reported AUROC values are not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance; additionally, PGS001777 has unknown covariates and a small validation sample (n=1,390), while PGS000704’s higher C-index (0.711) is a full-model time-to-event metric from a broad biomarker genetics paper and may not reflect PRS-only performance. These evidence gaps prevent a high-confidence selection. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. All candidates are direct matches on trait_efo and have broadly aligned endpoint labels, but none provide clean PRS-only AUC/R², so we must weigh heterogeneous, partly packaged evidence.

PGS001777 remains defensible as the best-supported direct-match because it is explicitly a disease-focused alcohol-related cirrhosis risk prediction study and reports both (i) a discrimination metric (full-model AUROC 0.671, SE 0.016) and (ii) a strong risk stratification contrast (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41). That combination provides two independent visible signals of predictive separation, even though covariates are listed as unknown and validation N is modest (n=1,390) and phenotyping_reported indicates a sex-stratified endpoint (“Cirrhosis (males)”), which limits generality.

PGS000704 is the strongest runner-up: it has much larger training/validation scale and a higher reported C-index (0.711) with conventional covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs). However, the reported performance is explicitly a full time-to-event model from a broad UKB-derived modeling context (snpnet multi-PRS), so the apparent advantage could be substantially driven by packaging and study archetype rather than a clearly demonstrated standalone PRS effect; its HR (1.18) is also a relatively modest per-unit effect signal compared with PGS001777’s extreme-quantile OR.

PGS004913 is highly on-construct (heavy drinkers; alcohol-associated cirrhosis) with conventional covariates and a purpose-built recent study, but the visible predictive evidence is weaker/less comparable overall (R²=0.029; OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4 with wide CI) and does not clearly surpass PGS001777 across multiple independent axes.

Given the stress-test instruction to retain the legacy pick unless an alternative is clearly better-supported across multiple independent visible axes, the evidence does not justify switching away from PGS001777. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed_pick: all three candidates are direct matches on trait_efo (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) and have broadly aligned trait/phenotyping labels. The legacy/proposed choice of PGS001777 is defensible on visible evidence because it provides (a) an explicit discrimination metric (AUROC 0.671, SE 0.016) and (b) a strong extreme-quantile stratification effect (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41) in an alcohol-related cirrhosis risk prediction context. Limitations (small validation n=1,390; covariates unknown; phenotyping_reported indicates a sex-stratified endpoint “Cirrhosis (males)”) are real but not a visible contradiction.

No alternative is clearly better-supported in a way that forces revision: PGS000704 has much larger training/validation scale and higher reported C-index (0.711) but that metric is explicitly a full time-to-event model with covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), and its per-unit HR (1.18) is modest; without PRS-only metrics, it is not clearly superior on the visible record. PGS004913 is purpose-built and recent with conventional covariates, but its visible predictive evidence (R²=0.029; OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4 with wide CI) does not clearly surpass PGS001777 across multiple independent axes. Therefore keep the legacy proposal.

TRIAGE: Plan for downstream comparison by clustering into (A) UKB snpnet sparse PRS family with clean PRS-only metrics and multiple phenotype definitions, (B) MVP diverse-population method-comparison family with strong full-model discrimination but less PRS-only separability, and (C) UKB ICD10 I20 models from an integration/metaPRS paper with only OR reported.

A) UKB snpnet (PLoS Genet) — keep multiple near-ties because endpoint definitions differ and metrics are clean/comparable:
- PGS001262: “Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina” shows the strongest full-model AUROC (0.807) and also has PRS-only AUROC/R2 reported; could look best on full-model but is a slightly different ascertainment than plain angina.
- PGS001261: explicit “Angina pectoris (time-to-event)” (TTE) with clean PRS-only AUROC/R2; important alternative if downstream prefers time-to-event framing.
- PGS001260: “Angina” (non-TTE) with clean PRS-only AUROC/R2; close sibling to 001261 and may align better with non-TTE endpoints.

B) MVP HGG Adv method-comparison set (PheCode 411.3) — keep the top-performing and close siblings because single-shot picking could be misled by small C-index differences and because these are strong direct-endpoint predictive signals even though reported as full-model C-index/OR (age/sex/PCs included):
- Strong/near-tie leaders by C-index with strong ORs: PGS005048, PGS005052, PGS005057, PGS005058.
- Very close runners-up worth head-to-head: PGS005051, PGS005050, PGS005054, PGS005059.
- Include at least one “same paper but weaker OR” comparator to avoid over-interpreting C-index alone: PGS005047/PGS005049/PGS005055/PGS005053/PGS005056 are kept on watchlist (still plausible, but appear weaker on the visible ORs and/or C-index).

C) Other direct-angina candidates with potentially misleading metric packaging (still worth comparison):
- PGS000703: direct “Angina” with full-model AUROC ~0.593 (age/sex/PCs). Looks weaker than others but has a much larger variant count and different publication context; keep as a sanity-check baseline and to avoid missing a model that generalizes differently.
- PGS004527 and PGS004457: both “I20 (Angina pectoris)” with only OR reported and covariates unknown; keep because they are direct ICD-coded endpoints and one shows a notably higher OR (metaPRS). However, lack of AUC/C-index and unclear covariate packaging could mislead a single-shot picker either way, so they need explicit downstream scrutiny rather than exclusion.

Overall downstream comparison should explicitly separate (i) PRS-only metrics (available for the snpnet UKB set) from (ii) full-model discrimination/effect sizes (dominant in the MVP and Commun Biol sets), and treat endpoint-definition differences (Angina vs TTE vs doctor-diagnosed vs ICD10 vs PheCode) as first-class tie-breakers rather than assuming they are interchangeable. Uncertainty: Key uncertainty is metric comparability across families: UKB snpnet provides PRS-only AUROC/R2 and incremental AUROC, while MVP reports full-model C-index and OR (with covariates) and Commun Biol reports only OR with unknown covariates. Small differences among MVP siblings (C-index ~0.752–0.767) may not be meaningful without consistent PRS-only reporting; similarly, the high full-model AUROC for PGS001262 may reflect phenotype/case-definition differences rather than a strictly better PRS. The Commun Biol ORs could reflect different scaling/packaging, so they should not be over-weighted without additional performance fields. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported variants include Angina, ICD I20, and PheCode 411.3). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the UKB snpnet framework scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.59) and PGS R² (~0.012–0.013) with basic covariates, making them more comparable than candidates that report only full-model C-index/AUROC or only per-SD OR without PRS-only metrics. Within this snpnet set, PGS001262 has the strongest incremental contribution (incremental AUROC 0.0098) and highest PGS-only AUROC (0.58683) and PGS R² (0.01304) among the three, with a direct doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype. However, confidence is limited because these snpnet models come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk per the provided domain knowledge), and several newer ICD/PheCode-based models (e.g., PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057 with higher full-model C-index ~0.766 and OR~1.48) lack clearly PRS-only metrics, preventing a clean, high-confidence comparison. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal (PGS001262) because it remains defensible and no alternative is clearly better-supported across multiple independent visible axes.

All candidates are direct matches on trait_efo=angina pectoris, but they differ in endpoint framing and in how performance is reported.

Why PGS001262 stays best-supported:
- Direct endpoint with explicit phenotype label: “Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina,” still a direct angina endpoint (not an upstream proxy).
- Strongest and cleanest comparable PRS evidence among the UKB snpnet siblings: it reports PGS-only AUROC (0.58683) and PGS-only R² (0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098), and these are directly comparable within-family to PGS001260/PGS001261.
- Also shows the strongest reported discrimination in its own record (full-model AUROC 0.80729 with conventional covariates listed), and has a larger validation N than the other snpnet angina variants (n=49,472 vs n=24,905).

Why the newer MVP PheCode models (e.g., PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057) do not clearly displace it despite strong-looking signals:
- They are direct on endpoint (PheCode 411.3 angina pectoris) and show high reported C-index (~0.766) and strong ORs (~1.48–1.49), but the visible records do not provide PRS-only performance or incremental metrics, making cross-family comparison ambiguous (their C-index is a full-model metric with age/sex/PCs).
- Within that MVP family, several models are near-tied on C-index and OR, so picking one over the legacy UKB snpnet choice is not “clearly better-supported” from the visible evidence alone.

Why other direct ICD10 I20 models are not preferred:
- PGS004527/PGS004457 are direct ICD-coded endpoints but report only OR with unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, limiting supportability versus PGS001262.

Runner-ups reflect the main plausible challengers: the strongest MVP ldpred score (PGS005048) and close siblings (PGS005052/PGS005057) on full-model C-index/OR, plus the time-to-event snpnet alternative (PGS001261) if a TTE framing were preferred. CRITIC: No clear mistake found: both the proposed_pick and the legacy_with_domain_proposal select PGS001262, and that choice is defensible on the visible evidence.

Checks against visible records:
- Trait alignment: PGS001262 has trait_efo=angina pectoris and phenotyping_reported explicitly angina (“Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”), so it is a direct match.
- Comparable performance evidence: Among the UKB snpnet siblings (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262), PGS001262 is best on the PRS-only axis (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683; PGS-only R2 0.01304; incremental AUROC 0.0098) and also has the highest full-model AUROC (0.80729). This supports the within-family preference stated in the rationale.
- Validation support: PGS001262 has a larger validation sample size (n=49,472) than PGS001260/PGS001261 (n=24,905), which is consistent with the proposal’s supporting points.

Why not revise to an MVP PheCode model (e.g., PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057):
- Those are also direct matches and show strong-looking full-model C-index (~0.766) and larger per-SD ORs (~1.48–1.49), but they do not report PRS-only AUC/R2 or incremental metrics in the visible fields, so they do not constitute a clearly better-supported replacement given the instruction to avoid re-ranking close calls and to avoid treating metric cleanliness as a veto in either direction.
- Within the MVP family, several near-tied options exist; nothing visible makes one of them an unambiguous superior to the UKB snpnet pick.

Why not revise to PGS004527/PGS004457:
- Only OR is shown and covariates are unknown; no discrimination metrics are visible, so they are less well-supported than PGS001262.

Therefore: keep PGS001262; legacy proposal is defensible and matches the proposed pick.

TRIAGE: Two clear study families emerge and both deserve head-to-head comparison downstream.

1) UK Biobank snpnet siblings (PGS001267 vs PGS001268): both are direct-endpoint for ankylosing spondylitis with cleanly reported PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) plus full-model AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, conventional covariates, large training (n~269k) and sizable validation (n~67k) in European ancestry. They are near-tied but differ in endpoint framing (standard case/control vs time-to-event), which can mislead a single-shot picker if the downstream target endpoint expects one framing; keep both for explicit endpoint-alignment comparison.

2) UK Biobank portability paper scores (PGS002089, PGS001876): same phenotype label, larger training (n~391k) but performance is reported as partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R², making comparability tricky. Still, these are clean PGS-focused evaluations with conventional covariates and are plausible near-ties to the snpnet scores; include at least the stronger partial-r candidate (PGS002089) on the shortlist and keep the penalized-regression sibling (PGS001876) on watchlist for method/variant-count contrast.

3) Taiwanese EAS GWAS-derived scores (PGS003420–PGS003424): all are direct ankylosing spondylitis endpoints with AUROC reported only as full-model (covariates unknown), and all share the same small validation size (n=1,298) and single-ancestry context (EAS). Because the AUROCs are high and tightly clustered across methods, they are prime candidates for being misleading if picked in isolation (possible covariate packaging / non-PRS-only reporting / small-N optimism). Keep the top-performing and near-tied method variants (PGS003420 PRS-CS; PGS003421 C+T; PGS003422 PRSice-2) on the shortlist for within-family comparison, while leaving the slightly lower-AUROC siblings (PGS003423 lassosum; PGS003424 LDpred2) on watchlist as plausible alternatives.

Overall downstream comparison should explicitly separate (a) endpoint framing (TTE vs non-TTE), (b) ancestry/transportability context (EUR UKB vs EAS Taiwan), and (c) metric packaging (PRS-only vs full-model/unknown covariates vs partial-r). Uncertainty: Key uncertainties that warrant preserving multiple candidates: (i) whether the downstream intended endpoint is time-to-event or case/control (affects PGS001268 vs PGS001267), (ii) how to compare partial-r (PGS002089/PGS001876) against AUROC/R²-based records without over-penalizing metric format, and (iii) whether the high AUROCs in the EAS Taiwan set reflect PRS signal vs covariate inclusion/packaging (covariates listed as unknown) and small validation N. Because these uncertainties can flip the apparent winner, multiple near-ties are intentionally retained. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS001268 has slightly higher metrics but is explicitly time-to-event, which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target; therefore PGS001267 is preferred. Remaining limitation: the selected model is still from a pan-trait UKB framework (a known generalization risk), and there is no clearly superior disease-focused, well-powered, PRS-only-metric-reported alternative in the provided set, so the overall direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than high-confidence. PICK: Keep the legacy pick. PGS001267 remains the most defensible overall because it provides clean, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination/variance metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.7265; PGS-only R² 0.0988) alongside full-model AUROC/R² with conventional covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large EUR validation (n=67,425). PGS001268 is a near-tie and slightly stronger on the reported metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.7346; PGS-only R² 0.1023; full-model AUROC 0.7488), but it is explicitly time-to-event (TTE) phenotyping. The UKB portability-paper scores (PGS002089, PGS001876) are also direct and have large training, but they only report partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R², making the predictive evidence harder to compare head-to-head against the snpnet siblings; among them, PGS002089 is the stronger runner-up (partial-r 0.0919 vs 0.0797).

CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed pick; the legacy_with_domain_proposal and proposed_pick are identical (PGS001267) and are defensible given the visible evidence.

TRIAGE: Direct-endpoint aortic stenosis candidates should anchor downstream comparison. PGS005252 is a strong direct-endpoint contender with large validation N, explicit incident-case phenotyping, and a reported discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus HR; however its reported performance is a full model with multiple clinical covariates, so it should be compared head-to-head against cleaner/leaner covariate-packaged alternatives rather than assumed best by a single metric. PGS005254 is also direct aortic stenosis (incident) with a simpler covariate set (age/sex/PCs) and a clear HR with CI; it lacks AUC/C-index/R2 reporting, so it is a plausible near-tie that could be undervalued if one overweights availability of discrimination metrics. PGS005255 and PGS005256 are measurement-labeled (mean pressure gradient / peak aortic velocity) but are evaluated on incident aortic stenosis with the same simple covariates and similar HRs; these could mislead a single-shot picker (label suggests proxy/measurement) yet may perform similarly in the same evaluation setting, so they deserve close comparison alongside PGS005254.

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores are endpoint-misaligned for the target trait but remain on the watchlist because they include large-scale evaluations and/or strong-looking metrics that could mislead if one focuses on metric magnitude without endpoint alignment. PGS004911 and PGS004910 (PRS-CS, very large variant counts, large validation N, reported AUROC/R2 and OR/HR) are the strongest of the misaligned group and could appear competitive on generic predictive strength; keep them for sensitivity/robustness checks. PGS000739 reports a high full-model AUROC but is heavily packaged with clinical risk factors and rare-variant carrier status, making it particularly prone to misleading comparisons versus PRS-focused models. PGS000778 has small validation N and specialized phenotyping context, so it is a weaker and potentially non-comparable misaligned alternative but still worth retaining as a low-priority comparator. Uncertainty: Within the direct aortic stenosis set, comparability is limited by heterogeneous metric reporting: PGS005252 provides a full-model C-index with many clinical covariates, while PGS005254/255/256 provide HRs (with simpler covariates) but no discrimination metrics. It is unclear from the visible records whether any candidate reports PRS-only performance, so downstream comparison should explicitly separate (a) endpoint fidelity and evaluation design, (b) covariate packaging, and (c) metric type (C-index vs HR) to avoid overinterpreting any single reported number. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254; plus related aortic valve function measures PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is the best-supported direct disease-endpoint model in the provided context because it is explicitly for aortic stenosis (trait_reported/trait_efo) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping ('Incident aortic stenosis cases'), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside HR=1.92. Main limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so it is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; competing direct-match PGS005254 has cleaner/basic covariates but lacks comparable discrimination metrics (only HR=1.64). This leaves some uncertainty, but overall the endpoint alignment plus stronger available performance/effect-size evidence favors PGS005252. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. Multiple candidates are direct-match on the target trait (aortic stenosis), and PGS005252 remains the best-supported from the visible records because it is explicitly labeled for aortic stenosis (trait_reported/trait_efo) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (“Incident aortic stenosis cases”), very large evaluation scale (n=446,895), and it is the only direct-match candidate here that reports an explicit discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a substantial effect size (HR=1.92). While that C-index is clearly a full-model metric with conventional clinical covariates (age/sex/PCs plus common risk factors), this packaging is not so unusual as to invalidate the signal, and there is no competing direct aortic stenosis record with comparably strong, multi-axis predictive evidence (discrimination + effect size + scale) visible.

PGS005254 is the closest direct-endpoint alternative (incident aortic stenosis; simpler covariates age/sex/PCs; HR=1.64 with CI), but it lacks any reported AUC/C-index/R² in the visible record, making it hard to argue it is clearly better-supported overall than PGS005252. PGS005255 and PGS005256 are measurement-labeled scores (mean pressure gradient / peak aortic velocity) despite being evaluated on incident aortic stenosis with similar simple covariates and HR≈1.53; they are plausible but are less directly aligned by trait label than the two aortic stenosis–labeled scores. All hypertrophic cardiomyopathy candidates are endpoint-misaligned for the target trait and are not competitive for a direct-match pick despite some strong-looking metrics. CRITIC: No visible contradiction: PGS005252 is the only candidate explicitly labeled aortic stenosis with incident-case phenotyping and it uniquely reports a discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus HR=1.92, with very large validation N (446,895). The main caveat (C-index appears to be from a full model including conventional clinical covariates) is already acknowledged and is not a clear disqualifier given the lack of comparable AUC/C-index/R2 reporting for the other direct AS candidates. Alternatives: PGS005254 is direct incident AS with simpler covariates and HR=1.64 (CI shown) but lacks discrimination metrics; PGS005255/PGS005256 are measurement-labeled though evaluated on incident AS with HR~1.53, making them less directly aligned by trait label and not clearly better-supported. TRIAGE: Downstream comparison should center on candidates that most directly instantiate the target trait label (arthritis) and/or provide strong predictive evidence for closely aligned arthritis endpoints, while explicitly guarding against being misled by (a) very strong performance on narrower subtypes, (b) time-to-event vs prevalence endpoint differences, and (c) full-model metrics that may include covariates or packaged predictors.

1) Direct arthritis endpoint candidates (highest endpoint fidelity):
- PGS001135 is the only explicit "Arthritis (nos)" score with clean PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC/R2 available) and large UKB development/validation context; it should be the anchor for head-to-head comparisons.
- PGS004477 and PGS004547 are also explicitly mapped to arthritis ("M13 Other arthritis") and deserve close comparison despite limited/less comparable metric reporting (OR only, covariates unclear). These can look deceptively strong/weak depending on how OR was computed and what baseline model was used, so they belong in the shortlist for careful metric-context inspection.

2) High-evidence arthritis-adjacent candidates that could win on predictive strength but risk endpoint mismatch (keep for near-tie evaluation):
- Incident RA prediction with strong time-to-event discrimination: PGS004873 reports a high C-index for incident RA with HR; although not PRS-only and endpoint is incident RA rather than generic arthritis, the predictive signal is strong enough to warrant direct comparison.
- Multiple RA scores with comparable UKB-based evaluation and/or cleaner metric packaging: PGS001310/PGS001309 (snpnet RA and TTE other RA), PGS002088 and PGS001875 (UKB portability paper; partial-r), and the method-comparison family with explicit AUROC/R2 (PGS004163, PGS004049, PGS004021, PGS004079, PGS004064, PGS004094, plus PGS004257). These form a dense cluster where a single-shot picker could be misled by differences in endpoint labeling (RA vs seropositive RA vs other RA), metric type (AUROC vs partial-r vs pseudo-R2), and covariate handling (many "covariates: 0" entries). Keeping several representatives enables a fair head-to-head on what is actually comparable.
- PGS004326 (incident RA; HR) is included because it targets incident disease and could appear compelling in a transfer setting, but its metric is effect-size oriented and embedded in a broader covariate model; it can mislead if interpreted as standalone PRS discrimination.

3) Candidates with evidence that can mislead selection (explicitly preserve for downstream scrutiny):
- PGS000194/PGS000195 show AUROC ~0.75 in a clinical outpatient differential-diagnosis setting with covariates that appear to be packaged probabilities (G-PROB_*). These can look very strong but may not represent standalone PRS performance; they should be compared carefully rather than ignored.
- PGS002745 (multi-ancestry RA; AUROC/R2) is kept because it is a different training/ancestry construction and could be competitive, but its reported metrics are full-model and may not be directly comparable to PRS-only metrics.
- PRSmix/PRSmixPlus RA scores (PGS004817/PGS004819 and SAS analogs PGS004818/PGS004820) report incremental R2 rather than AUROC and are evaluated in different cohorts; they can look weaker/stronger depending on interpretation, so they belong in shortlist as "metric-format near-ties".

Watchlist rationale: The watchlist retains (a) other arthritis-spectrum endpoints (osteoarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, juvenile arthritis, reactive arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis) that could be mistakenly selected due to high AUC in narrower phenotypes or different age bands; (b) strong non-arthritis endpoints (notably gout) that have abundant high-performing scores and could distract a picker if only scanning for large AUC/OR; and (c) additional siblings within method families where one representative is shortlisted but others might matter if the downstream PICK prioritizes a specific ancestry, endpoint (TTE vs prevalence), or metric type. Uncertainty: Only a small subset of the 101 candidates are explicitly labeled as generic arthritis; most are subtype/adjacent endpoints. Several high-looking metrics are full-model (or effect-size-only) with unclear covariate packaging, making direct comparability uncertain. The Commun Biol "M13 Other arthritis" scores (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack standard discrimination metrics here, so their true predictive standing vs PGS001135 cannot be resolved at triage. Likewise, the very high C-index for PGS004873 (incident RA) may reflect endpoint definition and time-to-event modeling differences rather than a universally stronger PRS. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait are present (trait_efo = arthritis), notably PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)") and the "Other arthritis" models PGS004477/PGS004547. Among these, PGS001135 has the clearest endpoint alignment to generic arthritis risk (phenotyping_reported: "Arthritis (nos)") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus a full-model AUROC (0.67424) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its reported performance more interpretable than candidates that report only an OR without PRS-only metrics. However, overall support remains limited because the PRS-only discrimination is modest and the other exact-EFO arthritis candidates (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack comparable performance metrics and have vague phenotype labels ("M13 (Other arthritis)") with unknown covariates, preventing a high-confidence best-in-class selection. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. For target trait = arthritis, the only candidate with an exact trait_efo match (arthritis) and an explicitly aligned endpoint label is PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", phenotyping_reported: "Arthritis (nos)"). It also provides the most interpretable, comparable predictive evidence among the direct-match set: both PRS-only discrimination/variance (PGS AUROC=0.53928; PGS R2=0.00291) and a full-model AUROC (0.67424) with conventional covariates (age, sex, array type, PCs) and a clear UKB dev/validation context.

The only other exact-EFO arthritis candidates are PGS004477 and PGS004547 ("M13 (Other arthritis)"). While they are also direct-match on trait_efo, they are less well-supported on visible predictive evidence: they report only an OR (no AUROC/R2), have "Unknown" covariates, and provide less clarity on endpoint/metric context, making it hard to justify replacing the legacy pick across multiple independent axes.

Many other candidates have stronger-looking metrics (e.g., RA/incident RA, osteoarthritis subtypes, etc.), but they are not direct matches to the generic arthritis trait_efo and therefore should not displace the direct-match arthritis score when the direct-match option is defensible. Overall, the selection remains DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the PRS-only signal for generic arthritis is modest and the alternative direct-match records lack comparable performance reporting. CRITIC: Both the proposed_pick and the legacy_with_domain_proposal select PGS001135, and this is defensible given the visible records.

- Endpoint/trait alignment: PGS001135 is an exact match on trait_efo=arthritis and has phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)", making it the most directly aligned candidate to the target trait among the visible records.
- Comparative evidence vs other direct-match arthritis candidates: The only other exact-EFO arthritis records shown are PGS004477 and PGS004547 ("M13 (Other arthritis)"). They report only an OR (no AUROC/R2), have covariates listed as Unknown, and provide less interpretable performance context. Nothing visible contradicts preferring PGS001135 over them.

- Metric packaging: PGS001135 provides both PRS-only (AUROC/R2) and full-model AUROC with conventional covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) in a clear UKB dev/validation context; no visible covariate-leakage red flags.

TRIAGE: Shortlist focuses on (a) candidates with relatively strong, directly comparable predictive evidence for asthma in sizable validation (e.g., UKB snpnet family with explicit PGS-only AUC/R2; Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto with very large multi-ancestry eval; pediatric asthma PRS with very large eval), plus (b) cleaner-metric or method-diverse near-ties worth head-to-head (UKB portability partial-r scores; PRSmix/PRSmixPlus incremental R2; incident-asthma time-to-event C-index/HR; incident adult-onset HR tertiles), and (c) a high-AUC childhood-asthma model that could look dominant but is likely heavily packaged with non-genetic predictors and small training—kept to avoid being misled by a single metric.

Watchlist retains: older/smaller-variant or heavily covariate-packaged models that may not be directly comparable but could still be chosen downstream (e.g., family/environment risk score packaging; early onset-focused score); records with missing performance fields (Sci Rep LASSO siblings); method-sibling clusters with modest AUC but clean reporting (GenoBoost set); Commun Biol “integration” scores reporting only OR without clear standalone discrimination; Nat Genet cross-population PRS set reporting incremental R2 only (some near the better incremental-R2 range); and the 2025 PRS-CSx multi-ancestry meta-analysis grid where R2 differs by evaluation ancestry (important if downstream selection is ancestry-specific) but is hard to compare directly to AUC/C-index records without additional context. Uncertainty: Many candidates are not directly comparable because they report different metric types (PGS-only AUC/R2 vs full-model AUC vs incremental R2 vs OR/HR/C-index) and/or differ in endpoint framing (prevalent asthma vs incident asthma vs pediatric/childhood asthma vs doctor-diagnosed vs algorithmic vs time-to-event). Several records also have missing performance entries (e.g., some 2023 LASSO records) or report only effect sizes without discrimination/calibration, which can mislead single-shot picking. The PRS-CSx 2025 set appears to reuse the same R2 within each evaluation-ancestry block across multiple GWAS-ancestry inputs, so downstream comparison may need to treat them as a structured family rather than independent signals. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Multiple direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present with varying endpoint definitions and study archetypes. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly disease-focused for asthma in a pediatric context (phenotyping_reported: "Pediatric asthma"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 985,837 variants), and reports a comparatively strong effect size (OR=1.57 per SD, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside a reasonable full-model AUROC (0.66) in a very large validation sample (n=391,820) with multi-ancestry evaluation. Key limitation: endpoint specificity is pediatric-only (not generic asthma), and covariates are listed as "Unknown", reducing comparability and preventing a high-confidence selection over other direct-match adult/general-asthma models (e.g., PRS-CS-auto PGS001782/PGS001787 or UKB snpnet variants) whose endpoints are more generic but are either framework-style or have less compelling PRS-isolated evidence in the provided metadata. PICK: Revise away from the legacy pick (PGS002727) because a different candidate is clearly better-supported on multiple independent visible axes while remaining a direct endpoint match.

PGS001344 is a direct-match asthma score with (i) explicit PRS-only discrimination reported (PGS AUROC 0.64568, with CI), (ii) stronger overall discrimination than most other general-asthma candidates in this list (full-model AUROC 0.66621 with CI; incremental AUROC 0.07977), (iii) conventional/clean covariate packaging (age, sex, array, PCs), and (iv) substantial training (n=216,121) and validation (n=19,857) within a consistent framework (UKB snpnet). Among the snpnet asthma family, it is the strongest-performing and most endpoint-specific to a clinically interpretable definition (“Asthma (diagnosed by doctor)”) compared with broader/algorithmic/time-to-event variants that show lower AUROC.

Keeping the legacy PGS002727 is less defensible given the visible metadata: although it has very large validation (n=391,820) and a strong reported OR (1.57), it is explicitly pediatric-asthma framed (endpoint narrower than generic asthma) and its covariates are listed as “Unknown,” making the reported full-model AUROC (0.66) harder to interpret/comparably trust versus the UKB snpnet record with clean PRS-only and full-model reporting.

Runner-ups: PGS002727 remains a strong direct-match option if pediatric-asthma specificity is desired and the OR is prioritized; PGS001787/PGS001782 are large-scale general-asthma PRS-CS-auto scores with decent full-model AUROC (0.64/0.659) but lack the cleaner PRS-only AUROC reporting and do not exceed PGS001344’s discrimination in the visible fields. CRITIC: Proposed pick PGS001344 is defensible and no clear visible contradiction found. It is a direct asthma endpoint with clean/standard covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and reports both PRS-only and full-model discrimination with CIs: PGS AUROC 0.64568 (CI 0.63475–0.65662), full-model AUROC 0.66621 (CI 0.65552–0.67691), incremental AUROC 0.07977; training n=216,121 and validation n=19,857 (EUR). Within the visible UKB snpnet asthma siblings, it is the strongest (higher AUC/R2 than PGS001341/PGS001343/PGS001346; far stronger than PGS001345). Legacy proposal PGS002727 is also a direct-match asthma score but is pediatric-specific (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) and has covariates listed as Unknown; its AUROC 0.66 is full-model and not clearly comparable/cleaner than PGS001344’s PRS-only reporting. While PGS002727 has very large validation (n=391,820) and strong OR (1.57), the endpoint narrowing + unclear covariate packaging make it not as defensible as the primary pick given the target trait is generic asthma. Therefore do not revert to legacy.

TRIAGE: Plan for downstream head-to-head comparison around three main “archetypes” that could each win depending on what PICK prioritizes.

1) Direct incident endpoint, large-scale evaluation (likely strongest generalizable evidence)
- PGS002755: Incident atopic dermatitis; very large validation (n=337,910) with time-to-event HR reported; genome-wide PRS-CS with very large variant count. Metrics are not PRS-only AUC/R2, but the endpoint is directly aligned and the evaluation scale is a major strength.
- PGS004587: Also incident atopic dermatitis with the same validation size and similar covariate set; smaller GWS SNP set (23 variants) and HR reported. This is a “cleaner/simple” alternative to compare against PGS002755 because it shares endpoint and evaluation context but differs strongly in model complexity/variant coverage.

2) Severity-focused endpoint with very strong-looking discrimination but potential packaging/metric comparability pitfalls
- PGS001773: Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis; reports very high full-model AUROC (0.93) and R2 (0.49) with covariates (age/sex/parental ethnicity). This could mislead a single-shot picker because the reported metrics are full-model (not PRS-only) and the endpoint is severity-specific rather than general incident disease; still, the magnitude is large enough that it deserves explicit downstream scrutiny rather than being dropped.

3) “Paradoxical eczema in psoriasis/biologic-treated” family (endpoint mismatch risk; keep as misleading-evidence controls)
- PGS003486 and PGS003459: Same publication family, same validation N (n=3,212), similar covariates (PCs 1–2), modest AUROCs (~0.57–0.59) but notable ORs. These are plausible near-ties with each other and are important to keep because their phenotype is construct-adjacent but not the direct target endpoint; they can look compelling via ORs despite limited discrimination and narrower context.
- PGS004903: Same paradoxical-eczema context and N=3,212, but reports a coefficient/p-value with unknown covariates and a biologically curated SNP set. This is especially prone to apples-to-oranges comparison versus AUC/HR candidates, so it should be retained on watchlist for careful interpretation rather than excluded.

Downstream comparison should therefore explicitly separate: (a) incident AD HR-based large-cohort evidence (PGS002755 vs PGS004587), (b) severity/full-model AUC evidence (PGS001773) versus PRS-only interpretability, and (c) paradoxical-eczema subgroup scores as endpoint-mismatch controls (PGS003486/PGS003459/PGS004903). Uncertainty: Key uncertainties to resolve downstream: (i) whether the HRs for PGS002755/PGS004587 are PRS-only contrasts or embedded in broader models (covariate adjustment is listed but not whether PRS-only metrics exist); (ii) whether PGS001773’s very high AUROC/R2 are driven by covariates/packaging and how much incremental value the PRS adds; (iii) how much endpoint mismatch (paradoxical eczema in a treated subgroup) should down-weight PGS003486/PGS003459/PGS004903 despite their within-family consistency. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 6 candidates map to the target concept via trait_efo=atopic eczema, but endpoint fidelity differs materially. Three models (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are primarily evaluated on therapy-specific/treatment-induced endpoints ("paradoxical eczema" in biologic-treated psoriasis), which is a weaker match for generic atopic eczema risk. PGS001773 targets "moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis" (severity-restricted) and reports only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.93, R² 0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates, making the apparent performance hard to interpret as PRS-only and potentially non-comparable. Two models (PGS002755, PGS004587) align best on phenotype (both report "incident atopic dermatitis"), and both provide comparable effect-size evidence (HR high vs low PRS 1.249 vs 1.153) with similar covariates; between them, PGS002755 is structurally stronger (genome-wide PRS-CS with 1,090,702 variants vs 23 GWAS-significant SNPs) and shows the larger HR, so it is the best-supported direct-match choice. Limitation: neither incident-AD model reports PRS-only AUROC/R², and the HRs are not directly comparable to AUC-based discrimination, so confidence remains moderate rather than high. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. Among the six candidates, the strongest direct endpoint match to generic atopic eczema is the pair explicitly evaluated on incident atopic dermatitis in a very large European validation sample (n=337,910): PGS002755 and PGS004587. Between these two, PGS002755 shows stronger visible predictive evidence (HR high vs low PRS 1.249 [1.123–1.391] vs 1.153 [1.037–1.282]) in an otherwise very similar evaluation/covariate context, and it is a genome-wide PRS-CS model (1,090,702 variants) versus a small genome-wide-significant SNP set (23 variants), which is consistent with a more comprehensive polygenic signal capture when the endpoint and evaluation setting are aligned. The other candidates are less direct on endpoint: PGS001773 is severity-restricted (moderate-to-severe AD) and reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates, making the apparent performance hard to attribute to the PRS itself; PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in a treated psoriasis subgroup, which is materially endpoint-mismatched for general atopic eczema risk despite having some association metrics. Overall, PGS002755 remains the best-supported direct-match choice, but confidence stays moderate because neither incident-AD model provides PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/R²), so the evidence is primarily effect-size (HR) based rather than directly comparable discrimination reporting. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed pick. Visible endpoint alignment favors the two incident atopic dermatitis models (PGS002755, PGS004587) over severity-restricted (PGS001773) and paradoxical-eczema-in-psoriasis subgroup endpoints (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903). Between the two incident-AD candidates, the records show comparable evaluation context (both EUR eval, n=337,910, similar covariates listed) with PGS002755 having stronger visible effect evidence (HR 1.249 [1.123–1.391] vs 1.153 [1.037–1.282]) and a genome-wide PRS-CS construction (1,090,702 variants) versus 23 GWS SNPs, making PGS002755 a defensible best-supported direct-match choice. PGS001773’s AUROC 0.93/R2 0.49 are explicitly full-model metrics with demographic/ethnicity covariates and a severity-restricted phenotype, so it is not a clear better-supported alternative for generic atopic eczema risk. PICK: Keep legacy proposal. PGS005168 remains the most defensible best-supported direct-match for atrial fibrillation on the visible record set: (1) endpoint fidelity is direct (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both atrial fibrillation, not a proxy construct or horizon-conditioned predicted-risk label); (2) it is embedded in a large, disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis context with extensive listed contributing cohorts and many performance records (record_count=45), which is strong independent support versus single-cohort/portability-style frameworks; and (3) it shows the strongest visible discrimination among the direct AF candidates (European eval C-index 0.8718, CI 0.8657–0.878) alongside a clear effect size signal (HR 1.6663; beta/SE reported). TRIAGE: All four candidates merit close downstream comparison because they form two distinct endpoint/metric families with plausible trade-offs that could mislead a single-shot picker.

1) Direct-endpoint vs broader endpoint trade-off:
- PGS001263 is the only candidate explicitly aligned to the target endpoint label (“Atrial flutter”) in trait/phenotyping fields, with clean PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC/R²) plus full-model and incremental AUROC.
- PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 target a broader combined endpoint (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”), with PGS001339 additionally being time-to-event (TTE). These may have more power/robustness but are less endpoint-fidel to atrial flutter specifically.

2) Metric comparability/cleanliness vs strength ambiguity:
- PGS001263 and PGS001339 provide directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² (both snpnet, similar training N, same validation N, similar covariates), making them a clean head-to-head near-tie where endpoint definition (flutter-only vs combined TTE) is the key differentiator.
- PGS001841 and PGS002050 come from a different publication family with larger training N and report partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R². That metric mismatch can mislead if treated as directly comparable to AUROC; nonetheless, these are plausible strong alternatives (same phenotype label, same covariate set, same validation N) and should be kept for explicit comparison rather than dropped.

3) Method/architecture and variant-count contrasts that could matter:
- PGS001263/PGS001339: sparse snpnet models (~2k variants) with explicit PRS-only AUROC.
- PGS001841: penalized regression (~4k variants) and PGS002050: LDpred2 genome-wide (~555k variants). Either could outperform in practice despite less directly comparable reported metrics; keeping both avoids over-privileging “clean AUROC” reporting.

Overall: shortlist all four to force downstream PICK to explicitly adjudicate (a) endpoint fidelity (flutter-only vs combined/TTE), (b) metric comparability (AUROC/R² vs partial-r), and (c) training scale/method/variant-coverage differences. A second uncertainty is endpoint definition differences (flutter-only vs combined; TTE vs non-TTE) which may change apparent performance even within the same cohort and covariate setup. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears either as the sole endpoint or explicitly within a combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all specifically “Atrial flutter”, making it the most endpoint-faithful direct match to the target trait. It also reports clean, directly interpretable PRS-only discrimination/fit (PGS-only AUROC 0.61716; PGS-only R² 0.02517) plus full-model AUROC and incremental AUROC with conventional covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a reasonable validation N (24,905 EUR selected).

LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Direct-match dementia candidates are present (e.g., PGS000929 all-cause dementia, PGS000946 unspecified dementia TTE, PGS001827 dementia, PGS002035 dementia, PGS004281–PGS004284 all-cause dementia, PGS004318 dementia, and PGS005170 incident all-cause dementia). All candidates are direct or near-direct to knee osteoarthritis (knee OA / gonarthrosis), but the strongest overall visible support for a standalone PGS on a directly aligned endpoint remains PGS002767: it is explicitly for knee osteoarthritis, uses a genome-wide PRS method (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants), reports a clear per-SD effect size with tight CI (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.30–1.40), and is evaluated in a comparatively large European validation sample (n=39,444) with conventional covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates).
